decision.summaryForCoordinator: This is a v1 with no predecessor, so nothing came free from a diff. The distinctive feature is quotation density: nearly every obligation reasons from a clause quoted out of state-class-contract.v11, so I tested each quoted string as a substring of live v11 rather than reading it. Six of six are present — the SUP-124 owner-concurrence sentence, the reserved monotonic trust-store sentence, the authoritative-evidence and PURGED sentence, the cache-identity-keys sentence, the g19.scope preview-classes sentence, and the namingStanding token — and the two G19-sourced quotations, dr113Split and leftoverNameNote, also match their live source. That matters because quotation drift has been the recurring defect class this session, producing findings in the FX-5, FX-6 and FX-10 chains; this artifact is the opposite pattern. The corpus equality holds twice over: namedCorpusNotAuthored is list-equal to live G19 v1 by ==, and the artifact's own secondary cross-check — that the same list equals namedCorpusClasses memberVerbatim — also holds when the memberVerbatim values are extracted from live G19 v1. The prohibition that needed real care is the grant journal, because the words must appear in order to be refused. All five SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL occurrences were read: one is the verbatim v11 clause requiring owner concurrence at recording, the others are negations plus a proposedLaterWork entry deferring apply-or-refuse to a later act. summary.grantJournalApplied is false and the obligation stays leftover. The same holds for PURGED across seven occurrences and envelope across four. Worth naming as the strongest external check available here: doctor-contract.v4's FC-RO grant-journal collision routes the DR-105 journal's state-class assignment to this very row, records it UNASSIGNED on both sides, and warns a harness author not to widen FC-RO's exception list before DR-124 places the journal. Had this join applied SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL it would have decided, from DR-124, a question another accepted contract expressly routed here as open — and without the owner concurrence v11's own text requires. It did not. Everything else checks: seven basedOn citations and eight recordedInputs files all match live with zero mismatches, recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head as the remeasurementClause demands, v11 carries a genuine dual ACCEPT with both verdicts opened and empty, G19 v1 is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED with no D-167 token anywhere in it, the DR-124 OPEN token claim matches live, the nine obligations partition across four buckets exactly with the four leftoverDesign-true entries matching the summary, only DR-G19 appears so no row is added, and MiB and 1024 are both absent so no D-006 unit is invented. Twenty attacks run, twenty refuted, zero findings. One standing note: v11's dual ACCEPT belongs to v11 and is correctly attributed there; this join can receive only a Claude verdict today because Codex is usage-limited until 2026-08-20 17:54, so this is a single independent review.
